audio.caption_accuracy.v1::zero_shot.text:
Listen to the audio and judge how accurately the caption below describes it.

Caption: A dog barks twice, then a door closes.

Rate accuracy from 1 to 5:
- 5: every stated detail is audible and nothing prominent is missing
- 4: all stated details are audible, a prominent detail is missing
- 3: a minor stated detail is not audible, or several are missing
- 2: a central stated detail is not audible
- 1: the caption describes different audio

List in unsupported_details each caption claim you cannot hear, and in missing_details each prominent audible event the caption omits. Keep every entry to a short phrase describing what is audible. Set abstain to true when the recording is too unclear to judge; then use accuracy 1, confidence 0, and leave both lists empty.

Return valid JSON only, with no other text and no keys beyond these:
{"accuracy": <integer 1-5>, "unsupported_details": [<string>], "missing_details": [<string>], "confidence": <number 0-1>, "abstain": <true|false>}
Every key is required.

generation.pairwise_alignment.v1::zero_s.text:
You are given two generated recordings, the first as candidate a and the second as candidate b, produced for the same generation instruction.

Instruction: Generate a calm piano melody that fades out.

State which candidate follows the instruction better. Judge instruction-following only, not recording quality, loudness, or duration, unless the instruction asks for them. Answer tie when both candidates follow the instruction equally well. The presentation order carries no information about quality.

Respond with exactly one label from: a, b, tie.
Respond with "unclear" when the audio does not support any of those labels.
Do not add any other text.

generation.pairwise_alignment.v1::pairwi.text:
You are given two generated recordings for the same generation instruction. The first recording is Candidate A and is reported as a; the second is Candidate B and is reported as b.

State which candidate follows the instruction better. Judge instruction-following only, not recording quality, loudness, or duration, unless the instruction asks for them. Answer tie when both candidates follow the instruction equally well. The presentation order carries no information about quality, and the candidate names are labels only.

Respond with exactly one label from: a, b, tie.
Respond with "unclear" when the audio does not support any of those labels.
Do not add any other text.

generation.prompt_alignment.v1::zero_sho.text:
Listen to the audio and judge how well it satisfies the generation instruction below.

Instruction: Generate a calm piano melody that fades out.

Rate alignment from 1 to 5:
- 5: every requirement of the instruction is audibly satisfied
- 4: all central requirements are satisfied, a detail is not
- 3: a central requirement is only partly satisfied
- 2: most requirements are unsatisfied
- 1: the audio is unrelated to the instruction

Judge instruction-following only. Do not reward or penalise recording quality, loudness, or duration unless the instruction asks for them. List in evidence the audible observations behind the rating, and in unmet_requirements each instruction requirement you cannot hear. Set abstain to true when the audio is unusable; then use score 1, confidence 0, and leave both lists empty.

Return valid JSON only, with no other text and no keys beyond these:
{"score": <integer 1-5>, "evidence": [<string>], "unmet_requirements": [<string>], "confidence": <number 0-1>, "abstain": <true|false>}
Every key is required.

interaction.turn_taking.v1::zero_shot.text:
Listen to the recording and assess how smoothly the participants take turns.

Rate smoothness from 1 to 5:
- 5: turns follow each other without awkward silence or interruption
- 4: one awkward transition, otherwise smooth
- 3: several long gaps or interruptions that disturb the exchange
- 2: frequent interruptions or long silences between turns
- 1: participants talk over each other or fail to respond

Judge only what is audible in this recording. List in evidence the audible observations behind the rating, and in disruptions each audible interruption, long silence, or unanswered turn. Do not estimate response times in seconds and do not judge the content of the conversation. Set abstain to true when the recording has fewer than two speakers or is otherwise not a conversation; then use score 1, confidence 0, and leave both lists empty.

Return valid JSON only, with no other text and no keys beyond these:
{"score": <integer 1-5>, "evidence": [<string>], "disruptions": [<string>], "confidence": <number 0-1>, "abstain": <true|false>}
Every key is required.

speech.emotion.v1::zero_shot.text:
Listen to the audio and identify the dominant perceived emotion of the speech. Judge only from audible delivery: pitch contour, loudness, tempo, and voice quality. Do not infer the emotion from assumed speaker identity or from the literal meaning of the words.
Label guide:
- neutral: even-toned delivery with little emotional colouring
- happy: bright, energetic, positively toned delivery
- sad: subdued, low-energy, downward-inflected delivery
- angry: tense, forceful, sharply articulated delivery
- fearful: unsteady, breathy, constricted delivery
- surprised: abrupt pitch rise with sudden energy change
- disgusted: recoiling, nasalised, heavily stressed delivery
- other: an emotion that none of the labels above describes

Respond with exactly one label from: neutral, happy, sad, angry, fearful, surprised, disgusted, other.
Respond with "unclear" when the audio does not support any of those labels.
Do not add any other text.

speech.overlap.v1::zero_shot.text:
Listen to the audio and judge how much of it contains two or more people speaking at the same time. Judge only simultaneous speech; back-channel sounds such as a brief "mm-hm" over a pause do not count, and neither does background media or ambience.
Label guide:
- none: speakers take turns cleanly, or only one speaker is present
- minimal: a few brief overlaps at turn boundaries
- moderate: repeated overlaps that are still easy to follow
- significant: frequent overlaps that make following the speech hard
- constant: simultaneous speech through most of the recording

Respond with exactly one label from: none, minimal, moderate, significant, constant.
Respond with "unclear" when the audio does not support any of those labels.
Do not add any other text.

- minimal: a few brief overlaps at turn boundaries

speech.recording_quality.v1::zero_shot.text:
Listen to the audio and rate the technical quality of the recording. Judge capture quality only: background noise, reverberation, clipping, bandwidth limitation, dropouts, and coding artefacts. Do not rate the speaker's delivery, accent, or the interest of the content.
Label guide:
- professional: studio-clean capture with no audible defect
- good: clear capture with only slight noise or reverberation
- fair: audible defects that do not prevent comfortable listening
- poor: strong defects that make listening effortful
- very_poor: severe defects that make parts of the speech unusable

Respond with exactly one label from: professional, good, fair, poor, very_poor.
Respond with "unclear" when the audio does not support any of those labels.
Do not add any other text.

speech.speaker_count.v1::zero_shot.text:
Listen to the audio and count the distinct speakers you can hear. Count a speaker once however often they speak, and count only human voices that produce speech. Do not count background voices that are part of an ambience and cannot be followed, and do not count singing or non-speech vocal sounds. Answer 0 when the recording contains no speech, and 10 when more distinct speakers than that are audible.

Respond with a single integer between 0 and 10.
Respond with "unclear" when the audio does not support an answer.
Do not add any other text.
